content.text:
Improve the release workflow:
- Add prerelease: auto under release: in .goreleaser.yaml. goreleaser will then mark -rc.N tags as pre-releases on the draft, so you don't have to tick it by hand.
- Add a short "Releasing" section to the README or docs/decisions.md: push a tag, publish the draft, never create the release from the release page. Without it, the next person will make the same mistake. The preflight failure only tells you after the tag name is already used up.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
version: 2

project_name: entire-rsl

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy -e

builds:
  - id: entire-rsl
    main: ./cmd/entire-rsl
    binary: entire-rsl
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/entireio/entire-rsl/internal/versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/entire-rsl/internal/versioninfo.Commit={{.ShortCommit}}

archives:
  - id: entire-rsl
    ids:
      - entire-rsl
    # entire plugin install selects assets by goreleaser's default naming:
    # entire-rsl_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz, .zip on Windows.
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    formats: [tar.gz]
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats: [zip]
    # Exactly one binary per archive. entire extracts the first entry named
    # entire-rsl[.exe] and ignores everything else.
    files:
      - none*

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt
  algorithm: sha256

# One SPDX JSON SBOM per archive, cataloged by syft from the Go build info
# embedded in the binary. They run before the checksum step, so
# checksums.txt covers them.
sboms:
  - artifacts: archive

# Keyless Sigstore signature over checksums.txt, which covers every archive
# and SBOM. cosign takes the identity from the workflow's OIDC token and
# writes certificate, signature and Rekor entry into one bundle. Snapshots
# skip this step (mise run snapshot).
signs:
  - cmd: cosign
    artifacts: checksum
    signature: "${artifact}.sigstore.json"
    args:
      - sign-blob
      - "--bundle=${signature}"
      - "${artifact}"
      - --yes

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-next"

changelog:
  disable: true

# Immutable releases freeze a release's assets and tag once it is published.
# goreleaser uploads every asset, signature and SBOM included, to a draft,
# which stays a draft until a maintainer publishes it. Nothing is uploaded
# after that.
release:
  draft: true
  # A re-run after a failure deletes the earlier run's draft instead of
  # leaving a second one beside it.
  replace_existing_draft: true
  # Stop before building when the tag already has a published immutable
  # release, which no run can change.
  preflight:
    fail_on_error: true

release.yml
name: Release
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      # Create the draft release and upload its assets.
      contents: write
      # Mint the OIDC token behind the keyless cosign signature and the
      # provenance attestation.
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # goreleaser reads the previous tag from history.
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Installs goreleaser, cosign and syft at the versions in mise.toml.
      # No cache, so nothing another workflow wrote ends up in a release.
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@f10502fc09dadecfefb962fff68ce77213930204 # v4
        with:
          cache: false

      # Uploads archives, SBOMs, checksums.txt and its Sigstore bundle to a
      # draft release. See the release section of .goreleaser.yaml.
      - name: Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: goreleaser release --clean

      # Stored by GitHub's attestation API, not as a release asset, so it
      # works on a draft and needs no change to the release.
      - name: Attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest@1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: ./dist/checksums.txt

      # Checks what users will check, before a maintainer publishes the
      # draft and makes it immutable.
      - name: Verify signature, checksums and provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          WORKFLOW_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
        working-directory: dist
        run: |
          cosign verify-blob \
            --certificate-identity "https://github.com/${WORKFLOW_REF}" \
            --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
            --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
            checksums.txt
          sha256sum --check --strict checksums.txt
          for f in *.tar.gz *.zip; do
            gh attestation verify "$f" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --signer-workflow "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/.github/workflows/release.yml"
          done

## 2026-11-04: Signed releases with SBOMs, safe under immutable releases

- **Context:** releases shipped archives and `checksums.txt` only, with no
  release workflow. The repository may enable GitHub immutable releases,
  which freeze a release's assets and tag once it is published, so nothing
  can be added after publishing and a published tag cannot be released
  again.
- **Decision:** `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs goreleaser on a `v*`
  tag. syft writes one SPDX JSON SBOM per archive, before the checksum step,
  so `checksums.txt` covers them. cosign signs `checksums.txt` keyless with
  the workflow's OIDC identity into `checksums.txt.sigstore.json`.
  `actions/attest` records build provenance for every file in
  `checksums.txt`. The job then verifies the signature, the checksums and
  the provenance. goreleaser uploads everything to a draft that a
  maintainer publishes, so every asset is in place before the release
  becomes immutable. Attestations live in GitHub's attestation API, not in
  the release. `replace_existing_draft` keeps a re-run from leaving a second
  draft, and `preflight.fail_on_error` stops a run for a tag that already
  has an immutable release. cosign and syft are pinned in `mise.toml`.
  `mise run snapshot` skips signing, which needs the CI identity.
- **Consequences:** a published release cannot be fixed. A broken one needs a
  new tag. Signing records the repository, workflow and tag in the public
  Rekor log. Attestations in a private repository need GitHub Enterprise
  Cloud.
- **Rejected:** signing each archive (the signed checksums cover them),
  CycloneDX (SPDX is goreleaser's default and what GitHub's dependency graph
  exports), uploading signatures after goreleaser publishes (refused once
  the release is immutable), and the mise-action cache in the release job
  (zizmor `cache-poisoning`).

## Development

Tooling is pinned in `mise.toml`.

```sh
mise install        # Go, golangci-lint, goreleaser, govulncheck, go-licenses
mise run fmt        # gofmt
mise run lint       # golangci-lint and repository checks
mise run test       # unit tests
mise run check      # fmt + lint + tests with -race; must pass before every commit
mise run build      # ./bin/entire-rsl
mise run snapshot   # local goreleaser snapshot into ./dist
mise run fuzz       # fuzz every target, FUZZTIME per target
```

`go test ./cmd/entire-rsl` runs the dispatch acceptance test when the Entire
CLI is on PATH: it installs the built binary with `entire plugin install` into
a temporary plugin directory and compares `entire rsl ...` with the binary.

Read [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for the repository rules: the read-only guarantee, how verification states are decided, and test conventions. Non-obvious design decisions are recorded in [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md).

[docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md).

### Releasing

1. Push a `v*` tag, for example `git tag v1.2.0 && git push origin v1.2.0`.
   A suffix such as `-rc.1` marks the release as a pre-release.
2. Wait for the Release workflow. It uploads every asset to a draft release
   and verifies the signature, checksums and provenance.
3. Review the draft on the releases page and publish it.

Never create a release from the releases page. Publishing makes a release
immutable before the workflow has uploaded anything, and the workflow then
stops at its preflight check. A tag with a published immutable release cannot
be released again, so the version needs a new tag.

content.text:
I've made both changes, but haven't validated them. `mise.toml` isn't trusted in this checkout, so `goreleaser check` and `mise run check` both stopped before running. I didn't run `mise trust` myself. If you run `! mise trust && mise exec -- goreleaser check && mise run check`, I'll fix anything they turn up.

**What changed:**
- **`.goreleaser.yaml`**: added `prerelease: auto` under `release:`, with a comment. Any tag with a suffix, such as `v1.2.0-rc.1`, is now marked as a pre-release on the draft.
- **`README.md`**: added a `### Releasing` subsection under Development:
  1. Push a `v*` tag.
  2. Wait for the workflow to fill the draft and verify the signature, checksums and provenance.
  3. Publish the draft.

  It then explains why creating a release from the releases page fails: the release becomes immutable before anything is uploaded, preflight stops the workflow, and that version needs a new tag.
- **`docs/decisions.md`**: two additions to the existing "Signed releases with SBOMs" entry. The Decision paragraph now mentions `prerelease: auto`, and the Consequences paragraph now describes the releases-page mistake and points to the README section.

I put the steps in the README because `decisions.md` records decisions and isn't a how-to. `CONTRIBUTING.md` would also work if you'd rather keep maintainer steps out of the README.

Nothing is committed. If you want a commit, the message would be `docs: document the release steps and mark rc tags as pre-releases`, with the Assisted-by and Signed-off-by trailers.
